plant_confirmed rule: true only when the quoted or adjacent page sentence ties manufacturing, fabrication or production to the named city or state. A footer address or a separate 'made in USA' line was not enough, so many attachment makers that are probably real plants stay false.

Quotes: all 86 non-empty quotes passed fetch_page.py --check against an HTTP 2xx response. I tested the checker: a nonsense string returns exit 1, but --check returns FOUND on a 403 page whose error text contains the string, so I re-ran every check and required status 2xx. The 28 rows with empty quotes are from search snippets, from pages that returned 403, 404, 502 or connection errors (Rockland, Hensley, Allied-Gator, Pengo, Bodine, D&E, Eagle Crusher, Fab Tec, Fletcher, Dillman, R/S-Godwin, Ox Bodies, Dakota Bodies), or from URLs never fetched successfully (TCI, Artisan, Ground Force, Broadwind). web.archive.org fetches via curl returned nothing in this run.

Deliberately not listed: Komatsu Peoria and Caterpillar South Milwaukee appeared only in an IndustrySelect snippet. IndustrySelect is a NAICS-coded establishment database, which the frame forbids. Phillips Machine and Interstate Machinery (WV) were dropped as rebuild-focused and seen only in snippets.
Truck bodies: on-road dump bodies are kept in definition as bulk-material haulers and flagged 'on-road' in note, so the coordinator can filter them. Service and van bodies were not collected.
Compact/skid-steer attachment makers are kept in definition and flagged in note where the page says so.
State 'unknown' with an area-code hint in note means only a directory phone number was available. The state is not established.
Output adds keys beyond the seven requested: reached_dry_point, counts, blind_spots. 'notes' is a list.
blind_spots: The buyer's guide lists brands, not plants, and over-weights compact and skid-steer attachment brands. Multi-plant parents (Paladin, Stanley Infrastructure, Astec, Terex, Komatsu, Caterpillar, Deere) resolve to an HQ, not to each welding plant.

Unbranded Tier 1 and Tier 2 fabricators that weld booms, frames, tanks and truck-body subassemblies for OEMs are invisible to dealer, marketplace and trademark angles. Supplier awards surfaced only D&S Mfg and Defiance.
Mining OEM and coal-equipment plants were only partly resolved. Marketplace manufacturer indexes (CEG, MachineryTrader) blocked automated fetches, so the auction/marketplace leg yielded nothing.
Search summaries skew to older trade press. Several expansion articles predate 2023, and closures (e.g. Cat Wamego, scheduled for mid-2025) may be missed.
